== Course of events ==

After being freed from his long rust and traveling onward with his companions, the Scarecrow confronts a realization tied to his past: having lost his ability to love the Munchkin girl he once wanted to marry, he now believes that happiness requires a heart, rather than the intellect he prizes so highly in himself. This conviction sets him apart from the Scarecrow's own outlook, since the Scarecrow still insists that brains matter more than any heart could.

The belief marks a turning point for Scarecrow, who resolves to seek out Oz and ask for a heart, framing his hope for happiness around this newfound need. It stands in direct contrast to the Scarecrow, who continues to hold that reasoning and thought outweigh feeling, setting up the differing goals the two companions will carry with them as they continue along the road.
